reviews.review:
This game was really fun at the beta stage and i really was hype to play more of it after it released. But after months of it being released, it doesn't have the charm as the L4D series as a whole has. Don't get me wrong this game is fun and all but the hype for it quickly vanished and it's not what it feels like. The higher the difficulty just makes it unbearable to play as you instantly wiped out even with a good team and deck build. And the versus mode isn't the best either, its a survival wave against infected players and survivors. 
For those that think about buying this game, I'd advise against it and get another multiplayer game to have fun with friends and against people

Basically left 4 dead with a bit more, although the inability to gain anything without playing with other people is a bad design choice and quite frustrating to those who would prefer to play the game on their own and actually have something to show for it.
I like it. its a good game. Wish it wasn't so repetitive but its still fun

This game is a dry pile of crap.

I loaded in, after checking the identity theft boxes, then it asked me to set a pile of game settings. Then it threw me into some outpost and had a bunch of NPCs all around that if I touched any of them I'd go deaf while watching some video about some feature of the game. All I'm looking for is to shoot some damn monsters. Okay, I skip the videos because I know how all of these games go. Now I just want to play a solo campaign to learn, but it says I must have other players? I have to? No solo? Fine. I guess I figure out how to look for a game and I put in RECRUIT because ITS MY FIRST GAME and it sends me to a game in the middle of some massive horde of zombies. I take over a BOT, because, hey, apparently bots are a thing so I have no idea why I could not play SOLO, and I immediately start shooting. There's special zombies doing all sorts of wacky stuff all around me, no idea what's going on. I start shooting and killing the zombies. Okay,  I killed like 30 of them. I see the path to go on and I head towards it. I barely touched the edge of this ledge and I'm suddenly hanging off the side of it waiting to get rescued.

Have these developers REALLY made left4dead? What is this pile of convoluted nonsense? Never touching this one, or these developers. Give up your jobs. It's over. You have no idea how to make a game. Way too many damn options and settings and a freaking town? Just start me in a FREAKING TUTORIAL. START ME THERE! Start me in a SINGLE PLAYER TUTORIAL. You don't even have to write a story. Just, like, don't just throw all of the options at me! I have no idea what was happening and then I got my guy on a ledge and messed up that team's game. I completely DESTROYED their game in 30 seconds. Why would you put a brand new player in the middle of a freaking horde event? I wanted to START at the beginning. I have no idea what way to go. I don't know the map. I don't know the guns. I don't know the zombies.

Quit your jobs. Go work retail. You're not meant to make a game.

Fun, if a bit grindy, co-op horde shooter. People need to stop comparing it to L4D, it's fine on its own. Nothing's gonna live up to the original.

It's like Salt & Sanctuary and Dark Souls, obviously inspired, but still solid on its own without the comparison.

I enjoy the simplicity of L4D, but Back 4 Blood is not a bad compromise.  Fun with friends.  Try to make the most bonkers broken build possible.  Cover the map in razor wire and sit back while zombies die just trying to reach you.  Become a blender and stab 6 times a second.  Burn everything to the ground with molotovs that give you molotovs when you kill zombies with them.  Use a sniper rifle... I guess.

This game had a lot of issues at launch, but the devs have addressed them and I think the game is a lot better as a result. The guns feel good, killing zombies feels satisfying, and the difficulties let you tailor the experience to your current needs. It's fun to play with friends, and almost as fun to play with random strangers.
